content.comment_body: I'm using a counter with an on-threshold that can be adjusted from an operator display. I want to make sure the input value can't go below 3. Setting a maximum value would be helpful too if possible. Thanks, [user_name]

It is possible, but you have to use a workaround. You need to set up an additional counter to ensure the value doesn't fall below 3, and then refer to this value in your main counter. Check the attachment for details.

Thank you for your response, [user_name]. I'm setting the on-value directly from the operator display, not by increasing inputs or using function keys. I'm unsure how to achieve this as there are no input limits like those found on more advanced operator panels. [user_name]

analysis.insight_summary: A user wants to restrict the minimum and maximum values for a counter threshold through an operator display. Since basic operator panels lack built-in input range limitations, solutions require creative workarounds. This highlights usability challenges and confusion stemming from limited input validation features on entry-level HMI devices, compared to more sophisticated models.
analysis.user_expectations: The user expects a straightforward option to define minimum and maximum limits for counter input values via the operator display, similar to the integrated range control available on higher-end HMI devices.
